caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a donut chart with two concentric rings, representing the distribution of samples across two ambiguity metrics. The outer ring corresponds to "Ambiguity Std" with four segments: a dark blue segment labeled 49.0% for Std: 0.0, a medium blue segment labeled 38.0% for Std: 0.47, a lighter blue segment labeled 7.0% for Std: 0.82, and a bright blue segment labeled 5.0% for Std: 0.94. The inner ring corresponds to "Max Ambiguity" with three segments: a light blue segment labeled 39.0% for Max: 1, a slightly lighter blue segment labeled 47.7% for Max: 2, and a very light blue segment labeled 14.2% for Max: 3. The chart includes two legends to the right: one for the outer ring mapping the four standard deviation values to their respective shades of blue, and one for the inner ring mapping the three maximum ambiguity values to their corresponding light blue shades. Percentage labels are displayed directly on each segment. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top-right, with the largest outer segment (49.0%) positioned at the top-left and the largest inner segment (47.7%) at the top-right.
